title: Two Countries One Heart (Chas McIvor)
style: Afro-folk mbira thumb piano acoustic guitar warm baritone male vocal Zimbabwe-Australia family journey 106bpm brushed drums storytelling celebration Shona language warmth
lyrics:
[Intro - mbira pulse, acoustic guitar joining slowly]
You carry a country inside you
When you leave it
You don't stop carrying it
You just carry two

[Verse 1]
She brought the red dust with her
In the way she says hello to strangers
In the way she stands in a doorway
Taking the measure of a room
She brought the msasa trees in autumn
The way the sky goes enormous in the dry season
The way a family sits together without needing
To explain why they are sitting together

[Verse 2]
He was already there when she arrived
This southern country in his boots and his manner
He didn't know the farm or the language
But he knew how to make someone feel steady
And somewhere between what she brought
And what he already had
They built a third country
The one you can't find on any map

[Chorus]
Two countries one heart
Zimbabwe in the morning
Australia in the evening
Two countries one heart
The mbira and the magpie
Both singing at once
Two countries one heart
That's the only map they need

[Verse 3 - Shona phrase, with translation]
Mufaro ndewose — happiness belongs to everyone
That is what she knew before she knew his name
Tinotenda — we are grateful
For the distance that became the same

[Bridge - spoken, unhurried]
The family left the farm.
That sentence has weight.
But here is the other sentence:
The family found Australia.
And Australia got lucky.
Jeff and Jill brought something real with them.
And Joel knew it the moment he saw Kerri.
You can tell.
The way you can tell in the morning
Whether the day is going to be a good one.

[Chorus reprise]
Two countries one heart
Red dust and southern rain
Two countries one heart
Joel and Kerri in between

[Outro - mbira and guitar together, fading]
Mufaro ndewose
Happiness belongs to everyone
Two countries
One heart
Yes
